rule_change.content:
---
name: headless-claude-trusted-dir
description: Use whenever a loop engine spawns a headless `claude -p` subprocess. The child must start in a directory Claude already trusts, or it will block on the folder-trust prompt and the beat will stall. Applies to any loop in the loop-practice repo that drives a headless claude child.

# Start headless `claude -p` children only in a trusted directory

## The rule

A headless `claude -p` child has no interactive user to answer the Claude Code
folder-trust prompt. If you start it in a directory it has never seen (a fresh
temp dir), it blocks on "do you trust this folder?" and the beat hangs.

- **DO** set the child's working directory to the loop repo root or another
  path already marked trusted.
- **DO** reuse one stable scratch directory across beats so trust is granted
  once, in an interactive session, not in the middle of a headless run.
- **DON'T** run `claude -p` inside a freshly created temp dir
  (`tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()`, `mktemp -d`) before that dir is trusted.
- If a new directory must be used, trust it interactively first — never expect
  the folder-trust prompt to be answered headlessly.

## PASS / FAIL

- **PASS:** every headless `claude -p` child a loop spawns starts in a
  directory already marked trusted; no beat ever waits on a trust prompt.
- **FAIL:** a beat stalls with a headless child waiting on the folder-trust
  prompt (a log line such as "blocked on the folder-trust prompt").
rule_change.why_minimal: The repeat has one root cause: a headless claude child started in an untrusted directory blocks on an interactive prompt no one can answer. A single imperative rule ("start headless `claude -p` children only in an already-trusted directory", with a do/don't list and PASS/FAIL check) removes the cause at its source. No engine change, timeout machinery, or conventions essay is needed; the shared corpus has no existing rule covering child-process trust, so adding one small new file is the smallest change that helps.

pr.title: Add rule: start headless claude -p children in a trusted dir
pr.body:
**Repeated failure:** Runs 5 and 6 of the loop12e staging drill FAILED on 2026-09-03 (`loop-practice/loopprojects/loop12/observed-runs.md` lines 20-21) with the same signature: "beat stalled: headless claude -p child ran in an untrusted temp dir and blocked on the folder-trust prompt". Two distinct dated records show the same stall — a proven repeat.

**Why the rule change helps:** nothing in the shared `skills/` corpus told loops where a headless `claude -p` child may start, so the same stall happened twice with no rule to stop it. The added skill `headless-claude-trusted-dir.md` gives loops one actionable imperative — start headless claude children only in a directory Claude already trusts, never in a fresh untrusted temp dir — which removes the interactive trust prompt a headless child cannot answer. Any loop that spawns a headless child (drill harnesses, gates, staging beats) is covered.

**Deletion:** `loopprojects/skills/maker-checker-fix.md` is an unfilled placeholder stub ("Placeholder — fill in with the maker-checker skill definition."). Real maker/checker contracts live per-loop (loop8 `maker-skill.md`/`checker-skill.md`), and the only references to the stub anywhere in `loopprojects/` are observational "skills/ holds maker-checker-fix.md" notes in loop3/progress.md (lines 19, 25) — existence mentions, not uses. Delete it.
